successCriteria.note: Layers load and merge repo > overall > built-in; a malformed fact is a diagnostic (DM-470/471/472 tests; DM-468 c1-c3)
get_context returns scoped, ranked facts within the budget and lists the omitted ones (DM-468 c2, c4)
The seven named commands (plus advance_sprint, claim_kanban_card, takeover_run and adopt_revision) return context for orchestrators; every event has a built-in fact (DM-474 tests; DM-468 c5, c6)
The kernel is 798 words; the runbook mapping covers every old heading and every rule (DM-475; DM-468 c6)
The Knowledge card registers the overall repository and shows counts, diagnostics and git status (DM-476; DM-468 c7 screenshots)
The runbook measurement table: old guide 8,515 tokens, kernel 1,313, per-event push 249-1,371 (DM-477; DM-468 c8)

outcome.summary: The orchestrator gets scoped context from built-in, overall and repo knowledge instead of one monolithic guide: an 800-word kernel, 44 built-in facts, push and pull delivery, the desktop registration card and the runbook. All six success criteria are met with evidence from the acceptance round.

title: Knowledge layers: the orchestrator gets scoped context from per-repo and overall knowledge instead of one monolithic guide
